A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GSI research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite reformatting and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark accuracies, runtime measurements, ablations, acceptance-rate analyses, and generated reasoning traces in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original Qwen3 evaluations, runtime profiling, and empirical divergence estimates in Section 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same likelihood-adjusted rewards, soft best-of-n selection, acceptance threshold, and target-model fallback. Added explanations and newly disclosed generation constraints do not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MATH500, OlympiadBench, Minerva Math, MMLU-STEM, and GSM8K with the same task coverage. Qwen3 configurations and the additional MATH500 divergence analysis introduce no new dataset, domain, or task requirements.

E2.justification: Both evaluate RSD, small-model S-BoN, and target-model S-BoN, and retain rejection-free GSI comparisons. SPECS remains an indirect comparison to published results. Newly discussed EAGLE methods are explicitly not evaluated.

E3.justification: v3 adds Qwen3-1.7B/14B with thinking disabled, a 100-step generation limit, A100 timing experiments, and divergence estimation using 50 MATH500 problems with 64 drafts per step. It adds throughput and component-level timing measurements. Figure 7 also labels retained beta-ablation timings as H200, revising v2's statement that all runtime experiments used H100 without establishing that they were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 extends rejection and acceptance analyses and beta sensitivity experiments to Qwen3. It adds an empirical check of draft–target divergence underlying Theorem 1 (Appendix C.5, Table 4) and a runtime breakdown identifying model costs (Figure 4). The original threshold ablations and reasoning case studies are retained.

E5.justification: The existing three-seed, 95% confidence-interval practice is retained. Appendix C.5 adds a Monte Carlo divergence-estimation procedure, with means, plus/minus quantities, and maxima in Table 4. The meaning of those new plus/minus quantities is unspecified; no increase in repeated-run counts is established.

E6.justification: The original Qwen2.5 accuracy tables and ablation plots are retained. Substantial Qwen3 results are added: at n=16, Table 3 reports average accuracies of 66.9% for GSI, 60.9% for RSD, and 69.4% for target S-BoN; Table 1 reports respective GSI and target latencies of 1.21 and 1.82 seconds per step. These are new configurations, not same-setting improvements over v2. Divergence estimates and runtime-component results are also new.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 substantively revises a central guarantee: Theorem 2's rejection-dependent factor changes from (1-p(u)) to (1-p(u))^(1/4), with a rewritten indicator-based derivation replacing the earlier independence argument. Associated algebra and the asymptotic remark are revised, and Section 3 restricts golden rewards to nonnegative values. Theorem 1 and the claimed O(1/sqrt(n)) rate remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements extend the empirical claim across model families and sizes, and the abstract adds up to 28% lower end-to-end latency. The novelty claim narrows from the first test-time scaling method with the stated distributional guarantee to the first speculative test-time scaling method. The central algorithmic and convergence claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 explains larger Qwen3 gains through the draft–target quality gap, identifies PRM cost as a latency bottleneck, and discusses hyperparameter transfer. It adds a practical coverage argument and cautions against using Theorem 1's loose bound for tuning. The earlier OlympiadBench-specific explanation for RSD's advantage is dropped; existing reasoning-failure discussions remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix B supplies consequential reproduction details absent from v2: dataset-specific system prompts, 512-token step limits, an 8192-token context limit, the below-0.1 reward stopping rule, and 45/100-step limits for Qwen2.5/Qwen3. Section 5 clarifies that PRM verification and target likelihood computation are not parallelized. These are newly documented details; code access and supporting libraries are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to EAGLE-2, EAGLE-3, speculative-decoding scaling laws, and the Qwen model reports. A new passage uses batching limitations to justify excluding conventional speculative-decoding comparisons, and the novelty claim is narrowed to speculative methods. The existing related-work discussion and positioning against RSD and SPECS largely remain.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain recognizable, with localized explanatory additions and revised experimental discussion. v3 introduces an implementation appendix and additional experimental subsections, moves detailed accuracy reporting into the appendix, and updates author, acknowledgment, and conference-header text.

P2.justification: v3 adopts the ICLR layout and substantially reorganizes empirical displays. Figure 2 gains Qwen3 panels, acceptance and beta plots expand, and new runtime-breakdown and divergence displays appear. Runtime tables gain model-family and throughput columns, while v2's main accuracy table moves to Appendix C. The workflow figure and original reasoning examples are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence beyond v2's single model pair through Qwen3 evaluations and runtime profiling, while Appendix B fills important gaps in prompts and stopping conditions. Appendix A.2 improves the finite-n derivation using a weaker rejection-dependent bound, and Appendix C.5 clarifies limits on its practical use. These gains materially improve empirical support, transparency, and reproducibility despite retaining the original method and benchmark coverage.
